rvis

Interactive charts with one calling convention, and shiny dashboards from a configuration file.

  • Charts: rvisPlot() draws interactive charts with about 30 plotting packages (echarts4r, highcharter, plotly, apexcharter, amCharts, billboarder, c3, dygraphs, visNetwork, networkD3, DT, …) using the same arguments: the data, the columns to show and a list of settings. Changing the package that draws a chart is changing one word.
  • Dashboards: rvisDashboard() builds a complete shiny app from a YAML or JSON file (or an R list) naming its inputs, outputs, containers and layout, with the R code of its outputs. Any function of any package can be a dashboard item.
  • Interactive charts: clicks on nodes, links, bars, points, table cells or map markers become shiny inputs: directly for 13 plotting packages, and for any other htmlwidget with a CSS selector, without changing the javascript of the packages.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("genpack/rvis")

The plotting packages are optional: install those whose charts you use, for example install.packages(c("echarts4r", "highcharter", "plotly")). See Get started for the full list.

A chart 

library(rvis)
deaths <- data.frame(age = rownames(VADeaths), VADeaths, check.names = FALSE)

rvisPlot(type = "bar", plotter = "echarts", obj = deaths,
         x = "age", y = list("Rural Male", "Urban Male"),
         config = list(title = "Death rates in Virginia", yAxis.label = "per 1000"))

# the same chart drawn by another package:
rvisPlot(type = "bar", plotter = "highcharter", obj = deaths,
         x = "age", y = list("Rural Male", "Urban Male"))

A dashboard 

name: Hello rvis
layout: page
items:
  page: {type: sidebarLayout, title: Hello rvis!, layout.side: [bins], layout.main: [hist]}
  bins: {type: sliderInput, title: "Number of bins:", min: 1, max: 50, value: 30}
  hist:
    type: plotOutput
    service: hist(faithful$waiting, breaks = input$bins)
runDashboard("hello.yml")
rvisDashboardExample()      # 40 example dashboards, including the apps of the Shiny gallery
